C0.note: Nodes are interpreted as voters and edges as votes. Committee selection is done by voting rules (MES, AV) applied to an election built from the graph.

C1.loc: Section 5, p.7; Theorem 1, p.5; Section 6, p.8-10
C1.quote: We now introduce axioms to formalize the intuition
C1.note: AX: proportionality axioms. AL: NP-hardness and polynomial-time results. SI: Euclidean synthetic graphs. EM: real-world network datasets.

C2.1.value: graph (network); outgoing edges as 'votes'/'support'; election profile (V, C, µ) with 'preferences expressed by the voters'
C2.1.quote: outgoing edges as their support for other nodes, or simply their votes

C2.2.quote: using approval ballots where µi (c) = 1 if voter i approves
C2.2.note: OTH: the input to the group selection rule is a directed graph. Edges act as approvals. Cardinal utilities are derived from centrality.

C2.3.quote: voters are more likely to prefer candidates closer to them
C2.3.note: In the Euclidean experiments voters have ideological positions and competence bias, separate from the edges.

C2.4.quote: Edges between nodes are introduced based on the distances between them
C2.4.note: Doubt between DIST and IDU. In the main model the utilities µ are derived from the graph and the rule is applied directly. Only in the Euclidean model are positions separate from the edges. DIST is listed first.

C3.1.note: No strategic behaviour by nodes is analysed. Strategic selection is only cited in related work.

C4.1.quote: it defines a utility for node u derived from including node v
C4.1.note: Utility is defined via Equation (3) as the expected number of random-walk visits.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: a cohesive group S is entitled to ⌊k · |S |/n⌋ representatives
C5.1.note: Proportional representation axioms and experiments on group representation.

C5.2.quote: We view a group of nodes as cohesive if all nodes mutually approve
C5.2.note: Axioms are defined on graph structure. Experiments use node labels and source groups, which are not related to held attitudes by any statement.

VOT.quote_behav: We will interpret nodes as voters and outgoing edges
VOT.note: Edges are exogenous inputs. No strategic choice is modelled.

claims.quote: fostering a stronger connection between voters and their representatives
experiments prove the potential for applying our methods in real scenarios
Both of our techniques show a significant improvement over the Top approach.

C9.2.note: The claims about voters' connection to representatives and real-world use need the assumption that edges reflect voters' actual trust or preferences, and that inputs equal held attitudes. Neither assumption is stated.
